test_title: SSC CGL 2024 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On: 12 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which is the National Mission for Financial Inclusion to ensure access to financial services, namely, a basic savings and deposits accounts, remittance, credit, insurance, pension in an affordable manner?

options.text: Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana

solution:
The correct answer is __**Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• ** Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana**

 
 
• Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana (PMJDY) is a financial inclusion scheme launched by the Government of India.
 
• Its objective is to provide access to banking services to all households in the country.
 
• The scheme was launched by Prime Minister Narendra Modi on August 15, 2014.
 
• Under the scheme, any individual can open a savings or current account with zero balance.
 
• Account holders are also provided with a free debit card and an accident insurance cover of Rs 1 lakh.
 
• Pradhan Mantri Jan-Dhan Yojana has played an important role in promoting financial inclusion in India.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana

 
 
• It was launched by the Ministry of Rural Development (MoRD), Government of India in June 2011.
 
• It aims at creating efficient and effective institutional platforms of the rural poor, enabling them to increase household income through sustainable livelihood enhancements and improved access to financial services.
 
• It is aided in part through investment support from the World Bank. 
 
• In addition, the poor would be facilitated to achieve increased access to rights, entitlements, and public services, diversified risk, and better social indicators of empowerment.
 
• The blocks and districts in which all components of N.R.L.M are implemented are treated as ‘intensive’ blocks and districts, whereas the remaining as ‘non-intensive’ blocks and districts.
 
• In a typical intensive block, the first 3 years are spent building the organizations of the poor by mobilizing them into SHGs, Federations at Village, Cluster level, and Block levels.
 
 
 
• **Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana**

 
• Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana relates to the skill development of rural youth.

 
 
• Union government on 25 September 2014 launched Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Grameen Kaushalya Yojana to train 1 million rural youths by 2017.
 
• It targets youth, in the age group of 15–35 years.
 
• It aims to provide them with jobs having regular monthly wages or above the minimum wages.
 
• It is a part of the National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM).
 
• National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM) is the Mission for poverty reduction called Aajeevika. 
 
• The Yojana was launched during the 98th birth anniversary of Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay.
 
• Earlier the Yojana was known as Aajeevika Skills Development Programme (ASDP).
 
 
 
• **​Swaranjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana**
 
 
• The Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) was implemented at the beginning of the 1999–2000 fiscal year to replace six other related programmes.
 
• The initiative was created as a comprehensive plan to support rural impoverished people who work for themselves.
 
• It is funded by the Centre and the State in a 75:25 ratio and is implemented by commercial banks, regional banks and cooperative banks.
